rationale: The ticket asks that the loop/goal/monitor/background machinery mark its pushed prompts so a client can tell them from user input, without changing what the model sees. The contract fixes the marker as metadata.machinePushed === true on the pushed text part (metadata is a persisted TextPart field opencode returns to clients, and unlike synthetic/ignored it does not remove the text from model context). One contract file per acceptance criterion, all driving the real plugin factories (GoalPlugin, MonitorPlugin, BackgroundTasksPlugin) and the real remote-control /api/send user route against a fake opencode client that records the raw parts of every promptAsync push: stillReachTheModel pins AC-1 (goal notice, loop prompt, monitor event and background completion each arrive via promptAsync as a non-synthetic, non-ignored text part); carryMachinePushedMetadata pins AC-2 (each of those four text parts carries the marker); userTypedPromptsStayUnmarked pins AC-3 (a prompt typed on the phone through /api/send is forwarded without the marker, with a marked goal push as the positive control); machineryOutputUnchanged pins AC-4 (the pushed bodies keep their exact wording and formats and the pre-existing goal/loop regression, cadence and terminal suites stay green). At base the suite is red for the right reason only: the five AC-2/AC-3 positive-control tests fail because no dispatch site sets metadata yet (plus the user path assertion already passes, as it should), and the AC-1/AC-4 guard tests pass because delivery and wording are today's behaviour. The full repository gate (npm test) was measured: its only failures are these same five contract tests, no pre-existing test turns red, so declaredRedTests is empty. npm run typecheck stays green.
